Request Logging

morgan('dev') prints one line per request/response — the access log a running API needs and gets nothing like for free.

Every request this API has ever handled, across five weeks of manual smoke-testing and the jest/supertest suite, has been silent — nothing printed to the console unless console.error in errorHandler.js had something to complain about. That's fine for a test run, but not for an API someone is actually operating: when something goes wrong in a running process, "what requests has this even been getting" is the first thing worth being able to see.

// Figure 6.18: app.js
import morgan from 'morgan';

app.use(morgan('dev'));

morgan('dev') logs one colour-coded line per request as it completes — method, path, status code, response time — to the console. It's registered alongside helmet/cors/generalLimiter, ahead of every route, so it logs every request this API receives, successful or not. 'dev', one of a handful of built-in formats morgan ships with, is the terse, human-readable one meant for exactly this: watching a npm run dev terminal scroll by while you work, not parsing a log file after the fact — a concern a real production deployment would reach for structured logging (a library like pino) to address instead, but out of scope for what this course needs.
